newsitem.title: GERMANY: German aluminium body sees no US action on tariff.
newsitem.headline: German aluminium body sees no US action on tariff.

text.p: United States talks on eliminating the European Union's tariff on aluminium mill product imports are no cause for concern in Germany, the general secretary of aluminium industry association GDA, Christian Wellner, said on Thursday.
Wellner, who was responding to a Reuters inquiry, said talks between the U.S. industry and the Washington based U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) were unlikely to bring action.

"The U.S. have been pursuing this issue for years, but from our point of view, the current practice was agreed in the latest GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade) round and changes should only be brought up in the next round," he said.
"We demand regulations should stay in place as long as there have not been comprehensive renegotiations."
"Besides, the U.S. operate a system of non-tariff trade impediments which would have to be mentioned in this context."
"If terms of trade are to be discussed, both the tariffs and these impediments, such as anti-dumping procedures, would have to be studied."
Producers in the U.S. and other parts of the world have long challenged the tariff which they say distorts trade.
But EU producers say it is necessary to offset dollar fluctuations and the effect of cheap eastern European imports.
